# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The baseline passes the supplied simulation and has 13 routed LUTs, 6 FFs, and no BRAM use. Setup fails at WNS −0.931 ns while hold passes at WHS +0.091 ns, so timing recovery is the first promotion requirement; once timing is feasible, the candidate must also use fewer LUTs than the baseline. The reported evidence does not identify the critical path, and the top module is only a wrapper around a frozen depth-3, 8-bit FIFO core.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the occupancy counter’s compare and increment/decrement control with a four-state one-hot occupancy register may shorten the FIFO control path enough to recover setup timing, at a possible FF or LUT cost.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the `sync_fifo_core` instance in `sync_fifo` with equivalent inline logic specialized to its fixed 8-bit, depth-3 interface, using a four-state one-hot occupancy register to represent counts 0 through 3. Derive `out_valid`, `in_ready`, `push`, and `pop` from that state, and update occupancy on push-only, pop-only, or simultaneous/no transfer while preserving the existing reset priority and modulo-3 read/write pointer behavior. Keep the memory unreset and preserve the combinational `out_data` selection, handshakes, and every observable cycle; do not add pipeline stages.
